Rashi on Eruvin 103b:10:1.hebrew: לא אמרו - באותה משנה יתור בגדים אלא במקום בגדים, אבל שלא במקום בגדים, כגון באצבע — לא הוי יתור בגדים:
Rashi on Eruvin 103b:10:1.english: They did not say - in that Mishnah [that there is an] excess of garments except in a place of garments; but [when] not in a place of garments, such as on a finger — it is not an excess of garments.

Rashi on Eruvin 103b:11:1.hebrew: ותיפוק ליה - בין גמי בין צלצול, משום דחייץ בין ידיו לעבודה. ואנן, (ולקח בעינן) ולקח הכהן וזרק הכהן בעינן, דמשמע: בעצמו, על ידו, ולא ע"י אחרים:
Rashi on Eruvin 103b:11:1.english: And let him derive it - Whether [regarding] a reed or [regarding] a sash, because it interposes between his hands and the [sacrificial] service. And we require [as Scripture states]: “And the priest shall take” and “and the priest shall sprinkle,” which implies: by himself, with his [own] hand, and not through something else.

Rashi on Eruvin 103b:11:2.hebrew: בשמאל - שאין עבודה כשרה בה, כדאמר בשחיטת חולין: כל מקום שנאמר אצבע או (בהן) [כהן], אינו אלא ימין:
Rashi on Eruvin 103b:11:2.english: On the left - For [sacrificial] service is not valid with it, as it says in [Tractate] Shechitat Chullin: "Wherever 'finger' or 'priest' is stated, it is only the right [hand]."

Rashi on Eruvin 103b:11:3.english: Alternatively, on the right [hand], not in a place of service - Such as on the back of the finger.

Rashi on Eruvin 103b:13:1.hebrew: ופליגא - הא דר' יוחנן, דאמר: "שלא במקום בגדים לא הוי יתור בגדים", ואפי' בגד ג' על שלשה משמע דלא פסיל:
Rashi on Eruvin 103b:13:1.english: And it disputes - This [statement] of Rabbi Yoḥanan, who said: "[Something worn] not in the place of garments is not [considered] an extra garment," and it implies that even a garment of three by three [fingerbreadths] does not disqualify.

Rashi on Eruvin 103b:13:2.hebrew: אדרבא - דאמר: במקום בגדים, אפי' נימא אחת חוצצת. ואע"ג דמשום יתור בגדים ליכא למימר, דהא לאו בגד הוא — חציצה מיהא הויא, דכתיב (ויקרא ו): "ומכנסי בד ילבש על בשרו", שלא יהא דבר חוצץ:
Rashi on Eruvin 103b:13:2.english: On the contrary - For he said: In a place of garments, even a single thread interposes. And even though on account of an excess of garments it cannot be said, for it is not a garment, nevertheless it is an interposition, as it is written (Leviticus 6): “And linen breeches he shall wear upon his flesh” — that nothing should interpose.

Rashi on Eruvin 103b:13:3.hebrew: ג' על ג' חוצצות - דכיון דבגד מקרי, הוי יתור בגדים. והאי דנקט בלשון חציצה — משום דרישא איירי בנימא אחת במקום בגדים, דלא מצי למתנייה יתור בגדים, דלאו בגד הוא:
Rashi on Eruvin 103b:13:3.english: Three by three [fingerbreadths] interpose - For since it is called a garment, it constitutes an excess of garments. And as for that which he formulated [the ruling] in terms of interposition — [this is] because the first clause deals with a single thread in the place of the garments, where he could not teach [it as] an excess of garments, since it is not a garment.

Rashi on Eruvin 103b:13:4.hebrew: פחות מג' אין חוצצות - דאיידי דלא חשיב בגד, יתור בגדים אין כאן, דלאו בגד הוא; וחציצה נמי אין כאן, דשלא במקום בגדים הוא, ושלא במקום עבודה:
Rashi on Eruvin 103b:13:4.english: Less than three [by three] do not interpose - For since it is not considered a garment, there is no [issue of] extra garments here, as it is not a garment; and there is also no [issue of] interposition here, as it is in a place where [priestly] garments are not [worn], and not in a place of service.

Rashi on Eruvin 103b:14:1.hebrew: אדר' יוחנן ודאי פליגא - הא דרבא, כדאמרן — שלא במקום בגדים, ר' יוחנן לא חשיב יתור כלל, אפי' בבגד גדול:
Rashi on Eruvin 103b:14:1.english: With [the opinion of] Rabbi Yoḥanan, it certainly disagrees - This [statement] of Rava [certainly disagrees], as we said: [for] in a place where garments are not [worn], Rabbi Yoḥanan does not consider [it] an excess [of garments] at all, even for a large garment.

Rashi on Eruvin 103b:14:2.hebrew: אדרב יהודה בריה דר' חייא מי נימא פליגא - הא דרבא, דאמר שלא במקום בגדים פחות מג' אין חוצצות; ואיהו אמר דצלצול קטן חייץ, ואף על גב דלא הוי שלש על שלש:
Rashi on Eruvin 103b:14:2.english: Shall we say that it disagrees with Rav Yehuda, son of Rabbi Ḥiyya - [Does] this [statement] of Rava [disagree]? For [Rava] said that not in the place of the garments, [anything] less than three [fingerbreadths by three] does not interpose, whereas he said that a small sash interposes, even though it is not three by three [fingerbreadths].

Rashi on Eruvin 103b:16:1.hebrew: צלצול קטן חוצץ - משום יתור בגדים. והיינו נמי כלישנא קמא, ואין בה חילוק אלא במילתיה דר"י. והאי דנקטי לה במילתיה דרב יהודה בלשון חציצה — משום הך פלוגתא דר' יוחנן, דלא מצי למתנייה משום יתור בגדים, דקאמר: פחות משלש על שלש חוצץ במקום בגדים; ופחות מג' לא מצי למימר יתור בגדים, אלא משום חציצה. להכי נקט לה לכולה בלשון חציצה:
Rashi on Eruvin 103b:16:1.english: A small sash interposes - [He means it is prohibited] on account of an excess of garments. And this is also like the first version, and there is no difference in it except in the statement of Rabbi Yoḥanan. And as for that which they formulated it in the statement of Rav Yehuda using the language of interposition — [it is] because of this dispute of Rabbi Yoḥanan, who could not have stated [his ruling] on account of an excess of garments, as he says: [A piece of fabric] less than three by three [fingerbreadths] interposes in the place of garments; and [regarding fabric] less than three [by three], he could not say [it is prohibited because of] an excess of garments, but rather on account of interposition. Therefore, [the Gemara] formulated all of it using the language of interposition.

Rashi on Eruvin 103b:1:1.hebrew: מאי היא - מנא תימרא דמודי ר' אליעזר דכמה דאפשר לשנויי משנינן? דתניא: כהן שעלתה בו יבלת וכו':
Rashi on Eruvin 103b:1:1.english: What is it? - From where do you say that Rabbi Eliezer concedes that as much as it is possible to alter [the manner of performance], we alter [it]? As it was taught [in a baraita]: “A priest who developed a wart,” etc.

Rashi on Eruvin 103b:1:2.hebrew: בשיניו אין - דשבות הוא, בכלי לא. ואפי' בשיניו — חבירו אין, ואיהו לא, דחבירו לא מתקן ליה שפיר. והכי אמר במסכת שבת בפרק המצניע, דפליגי רבי אליעזר ורבנן בנוטל צפורניו זו בזו או בשיניו, שר"א מחייב חטאת וחכמים אוסרין משום שבות; ואוקימנא התם דכי מחייב ר"א — בנוטל לעצמו, אבל לחבירו — דברי הכל פטור:
Rashi on Eruvin 103b:1:2.english: With his teeth, yes - For it is a rabbinic prohibition [shevut]; with an instrument, no. And even with his teeth: his fellow, yes, but he himself, no, because his fellow does not fix it well. And so [the Gemara] says in Tractate Shabbat in the chapter [entitled] HaMatzni’a, that Rabbi Eliezer and the Rabbis disagree regarding one who removes his nails with each other or with his teeth, where Rabbi Eliezer deems [him] liable to a sin-offering and the Sages prohibit [it] as a rabbinic prohibition [shevut]; and we established there that when Rabbi Eliezer deems [him] liable, [it is specifically] when he removes [them] for himself, but for his fellow, everyone agrees [that he is] exempt.

Rashi on Eruvin 103b:2:1.hebrew: מני - הא דקאמר: בכלי לא, ובעצמו לא:
Rashi on Eruvin 103b:2:1.english: Whose [opinion is this]? - [This refers to] that which [the Gemara] said: With an implement, no; and by himself, no.

Rashi on Eruvin 103b:2:2.hebrew: אילימא רבנן - דאמרי מכשירי מצוה לא דחו אב מלאכה, ואשמעינן דשבות דחו — כגון בשיניו בחבירו, וכגון שעלתה לו בשבת, דלא אפשר ליה למשקליה מאתמול:
Rashi on Eruvin 103b:2:2.english: If you say [it is] the Rabbis - Who say that the preliminaries of a mitzvah do not override a primary category of labor, and [the baraita] teaches us that they do override a rabbinic prohibition — such as with his teeth [and by] his fellow; and such as [a case where] it grew on him on Shabbat, so that it was not possible for him to remove it yesterday.

Rashi on Eruvin 103b:2:3.hebrew: כיון דאמרי רבנן - לגבי דבר הרשות, דנוטל לעצמו זו בזו או בשיניו, אין כאן אלא משום שבות:
Rashi on Eruvin 103b:2:3.english: Since the Rabbis say - Regarding an optional matter, that one who removes [it] for himself — [using] one [hand] with the other or with his teeth — there is only [a prohibition] here due to a rabbinic decree.

Rashi on Eruvin 103b:2:4.hebrew: הכא - דקשרו בחבירו משום שבות דמקדש, לישתרי נמי לעצמו, דהא איהו גופיה נמי שבות הוא:
Rashi on Eruvin 103b:2:4.english: Here - Where they permitted [de-ka sheru, cutting the wart] by his fellow [priest] because of [the suspension of] a rabbinic prohibition [shevut] in the Temple, let it also be permitted for [the priest] himself, since he himself [cutting it off with his teeth] is also [only] a rabbinic prohibition.

Rashi on Eruvin 103b:3:1.hebrew: אלא לאו ר' אליעזר היא - דאמר בנוטל בשיניו לעצמו דעלמא, שלא למצוה, דחייב חטאת. ומש"ה, ה"נ, כיון דאפשר בחבירו — דהוי שבות — לא שרינן ליה למידחי אב מלאכה ולמשקליה לנפשיה. ואע"ג דאמר ר"א מכשירי מצוה דוחין אב מלאכה, כמה דאפשר לשנויי — משנינן:
Rashi on Eruvin 103b:3:1.english: Rather, is it not Rabbi Eliezer? - For he said regarding one who removes [a wart] with his teeth for himself in general, not for a mitzvah, that he is liable [to bring] a sin-offering. And because of this, here too, since it is possible [for it to be done] by his fellow [priest] — which is [only] a rabbinic prohibition (shevut) — we do not permit him to override a primary category of labor (av melakha) and remove it himself. And even though Rabbi Eliezer said [that the] preparations for a mitzvah override a primary category of labor, as much as it is possible to alter [the manner of performance to avoid a Torah violation], we alter it.

Rashi on Eruvin 103b:4:1.hebrew: לעולם רבנן - דאי לר' אליעזר, לא בעי שינוי, ואפילו לעצמו ואפילו בכלי שרי. ודקשיא לרבנן: כיון דנוטל לעצמו נמי שבות הוא, נישקליה איהו לנפשיה:
Rashi on Eruvin 103b:4:1.english: Actually, the Rabbis - For if [it were according] to Rabbi Eliezer, he does not require an alteration, and [it would be] permitted even [for the priest to remove it] himself and even with an instrument. And as for that which was difficult according to the Rabbis: Since removing [it] for himself is also [only] a rabbinic prohibition, let him remove it himself?

Rashi on Eruvin 103b:4:2.hebrew: אי דעלתה לו בכריסו - מקום שאפשר לו ליטלה בידו או בשיניו, הכי נמי:
Rashi on Eruvin 103b:4:2.english: If it grew on his abdomen - [That is,] a place where it is possible for him to remove it with his hand or with his teeth, indeed so [he may remove it himself]:

Rashi on Eruvin 103b:6:1.hebrew: הכי גרסינן ואי רבנן לישקליה ניהליה ביד ותפשוט דר"א וכו' - כלומר, אי אמרת בשלמא ר"א היא, ומשום שינוי — מתוקמא שפיר, כמו שמתרץ לקמיה. אלא אי אמרת רבנן, וטעמא דבכלי לא משום דמכשירין לא דחו אב מלאכה, ורבנן אשבות הוא דמהדרי — נהי דאיהו גופיה משניה ליה דלא אפשר למשקליה, דבגבו הוא, חבירו מיהא לאשמעינן דנוטלה ביד, דהא ידו נמי שבות היא! והכי שפיר למתני, דשמעינן מיניה תרתי: חדא — דמכשירין שבות דחו, ולא אב מלאכה, כדמשמע לן השתא; ועוד שמעינן מינה, מדשרי ליה ביד ולא בכלי, דהכא הוא כדר"א, דאמר התם בפרק המצניע (שבת דף צד:) מחלוקת ביד, אבל בכלי — מודו רבנן דחייב חטאת, דחשבינן ליה תולדה דגוזז את הצמר, שהוא חותך מן המחובר לבעלי חיים. אבל השתא, לא מצינו למיפשטיה מינה ולמידק דהא בכלי לא משום דאב מלאכה הוא, דהא ביד נמי שבות הוא, ולא קשרי ליה:
Rashi on Eruvin 103b:6:1.english: This is the textual reading: "And if it is the Rabbis, let him remove it for him by hand, and resolve [the dilemma in accordance with] Rabbi Elazar, etc." - That is to say: Granted, if you say it is [in accordance with] Rabbi Eliezer, and [the reason it is forbidden with an instrument is] because of an alteration, it is well established, as [the Gemara] answers below. But if you say it is [in accordance with] the Rabbis, and the reason that [it may] not [be removed] with an instrument is because mitzvah preparations do not override a primary category of labor, and the Rabbis are seeking [to avoid] a rabbinic prohibition — granted that he himself altered it [by having another remove it], because it was not possible [for him] to remove it [himself], as it is on his back; nevertheless, let [the baraita] teach us that his fellow [priest] removes it by hand, for [doing so with] his hand is also a rabbinic prohibition! And it would have been more fitting to teach it this way, for we would learn two things from it: First, that mitzvah preparations override a rabbinic prohibition and not a primary category of labor, as is implied to us now; and furthermore, we would learn from it — since it permitted it to him by hand and not with an instrument — that this [case] here is in accordance with Rabbi Elazar, who said there in the chapter [entitled] HaMatzni'a (Shabbat 94b): "The dispute is [regarding removing it] by hand, but with an instrument, the Rabbis concede that he is liable to bring a sin-offering," for we consider it a derivative of shearing wool, since he severs [something] attached to a living creature. But now [with the baraita's current wording], we cannot resolve it from it and infer that with an instrument [it is forbidden] because it is a primary category of labor, for [removing it] by hand is also a rabbinic prohibition, and [the baraita] did not permit it for him.

Rashi on Eruvin 103b:7:1.hebrew: ולטעמיך לר"א נמי - נהי דטעמא משום שנוי, הוה נשקליה ניהליה ביד; דהא איכא שנוי, דמודה ר"א בנוטל לחבירו שאינו אלא שבות:
Rashi on Eruvin 103b:7:1.english: And according to your reasoning, according to Rabbi Eliezer as well - Granted that the reason is because of a modification, let [another priest] remove it for him by hand, for there is a modification [here as well], as Rabbi Eliezer concedes regarding one who removes [a wart] for his fellow that it is only a rabbinic prohibition.

Rashi on Eruvin 103b:7:2.hebrew: אי אמרת בשלמא ר"א - לגבי מכשירי מצוה, שבות ואיסור דאורייתא היתר משוי להו. וטעמא — משום דאפשר לשנויי משנינן: כי היכי דמשנינן מאב מלאכה לשבות, משנינן נמי משבות החמורה לשבות הקלה. הלכך, יד חמורה משינים, דאורחיה בהכי ודומה לכלי, ואיכא למגזר בה טפי — יד אטו כלי:
Rashi on Eruvin 103b:7:2.english: Granted, if you say [that it is according to] Rabbi Eliezer - With regard to the preparations for a mitzvah, he treats [both] a rabbinic prohibition and a Torah prohibition as permitted. And the reason [that he required an alteration] is that where it is possible to alter [the manner of performance], we alter [it]: just as we alter [it] from a primary category of labor to a rabbinic prohibition, we also alter [it] from a strict rabbinic prohibition to a lenient rabbinic prohibition. Therefore, [removal by] hand is stricter than [with] teeth, for that is the usual way and it resembles [using] an instrument, and there is more [reason] to issue a decree regarding it — [forbidding removal by] hand due to [the concern that one might use] an instrument.

Rashi on Eruvin 103b:7:3.hebrew: אלא אי רבנן - וטעמייהו משום דאב מלאכה לא מידחי, למה להו לאהדורי (אלא) אשבות כל דהו:
Rashi on Eruvin 103b:7:3.english: Rather, if [it is according to] the Rabbis - and their reasoning is that a primary category of labor is not overridden, why would they need to seek out (only) a minimal rabbinic prohibition?

Rashi on Eruvin 103b:7:4.english: And there is nothing further - To raise any objection.

Rashi on Eruvin 103b:8:1.hebrew: כורך עליה גמי - ואע"פ שהגמי מרפא את המכה, הואיל והשתא מיהא צורך עבודה היא — דלאו אורח ארעא שתראה מכתו עם העבודה — מכסה אותה בגמי:
Rashi on Eruvin 103b:8:1.english: He wraps a reed around it - And even though the reed heals the wound, since now, at any rate, it is for the needs of the [Temple] service — as it is not proper conduct for his wound to be visible during the service — he covers it with a reed:

Rashi on Eruvin 103b:8:2.hebrew: אבל לא במדינה - שמרפא בשבת, ורפואה בשבת שבות היא, ואסור:
Rashi on Eruvin 103b:8:2.english: But not in the country - For [the reed] heals on Shabbat, and medical treatment on Shabbat is a rabbinic decree [shevut], and [therefore] forbidden.

Rashi on Eruvin 103b:8:3.english: And if to draw blood - That he binds it tightly with a reed in order to draw out its blood.

Rashi on Eruvin 103b:8:4.hebrew: כאן וכאן אסור - שאין זה צורך עבודה; ועוד, דהוה ליה חובל, ואב מלאכה לא משתרי לגבייהו:
Rashi on Eruvin 103b:8:4.english: In both [places it is] prohibited - For this is not a need of the [Temple] service; and furthermore, it is [an act of] causing a wound, and a primary category of labor is not permitted for them.

Rashi on Eruvin 103b:9:1.hebrew: צלצול קטן - אזור קטן נאה, כמו "היא חגרה בצלצול (קטן)" דסוטה (דף ט:), ובלע"ז בנדי"ל:
Rashi on Eruvin 103b:9:1.english: A small sash - A small, fine belt, as in: "She girded [herself] with a sash" in Sotah (9b); and in Old French, bendel [a band or belt].

Rashi on Eruvin 103b:9:2.hebrew: הוי יתור בגדים - ותניא בשחיטת קדשים בפרק שני (זבחים דף יח.): לבש שני מכנסים, שני אבנטים, חסר אחת או יותר אחת, או שהיתה לו רטיה על בשרו תחת בגדו, ועבד עבודה — עבודתו פסולה. ויליף לה התם מקראי: "בני אהרן הכהנים" — בכהונם, כלומר: בבגדי הדיוט הזקוקין להם; כהן הדיוט שלבש בגדי כהן גדול ועבד — עבודתו פסולה, דהיינו יתור בגדים:
Rashi on Eruvin 103b:9:2.english: Is considered an extra garment - And it was taught in Shechitat Kodashim, in the second chapter (Zevachim 18a): [If a priest] wore two pairs of trousers [or] two sashes, [or was] lacking one [garment] or [wore] one extra, or had a bandage on his flesh under his garment, and performed service — his service is disqualified. And [the Gemara] derives it there from verses: "The sons of Aaron the priests" — in their priesthood, that is to say, in the garments of an ordinary [priest] which are required for them; [meaning that] an ordinary priest who wore the garments of a High Priest and performed service — his service is disqualified, which is [the disqualification of] an extra garment.

Tosafot on Eruvin 103b:2:1.hebrew: מה לי הוא ומה לי חבירו - וא"ת: וכר' אליעזר מי ניחא? והא לא שרי הכא אלא בשיניו, ובמתני' שרי ביד — מדקתני: "אם בכלי כאן וכאן אסור", משמע: הא ביד שרי! וי"ל: דגבי בהמה, דאיכא מיאוס לחתוך בשיניו, לא הוצרכו לחתוך בשיניו אלא ביד. וא"ת: והיכי מצינו למימר אליבא דר"א דהיכא דאפשר לשנויי משנינן? והא קאמר בפרק אם לא הביא (שבת דף קל.) דמביא סכין למול אפי' דרך רה"ר, אע"ג דאפשר לשנויי ולהביאו דרך גגות וקרפיפות וחצירות! וי"ל: דהתם מקצר דרכו לילך דרך רה"ר, אבל הכא, דיכול לחותכו ביד כמו בכלי, מודה רי אליעזר דמשנינן:
Tosafot on Eruvin 103b:2:1.english: "What is the difference to me whether it is he himself or what is the difference to me whether it is his fellow?" - And if you say: And according to Rabbi Eliezer, does it work out well? Behold, here [in the baraita] it only permits [cutting it off] with his teeth, whereas in the Mishnah it permits [cutting it off] by hand — since it teaches: "If with an instrument, both here and there it is forbidden," which implies that by hand it is permitted! And one can say: In the case of an animal, where there is disgust in cutting [it] with one's teeth, they did not require [one] to cut [it] with his teeth, but rather [permitted it] by hand. And if you say: And how can we say according to Rabbi Eliezer that wherever it is possible to alter [the manner of performing an action], we alter [it]? Behold, he says in the chapter [entitled] Im Lo Hevi (Shabbat 130a) that one may bring a circumcision knife even through the public domain, even though it is possible to alter [it] and bring it through roofs, enclosures, and courtyards! And one can say: There, walking through the public domain shortens his route; but here, where he is able to cut it by hand just as [well as] with an instrument, Rabbi Eliezer concedes that we alter [the manner of doing it].

Tosafot on Eruvin 103b:5:1.hebrew: שעלתה לו נשיכה בגבו - תימה, דלשמעינן רבותא טפי: כגון שעלתה במקום שיכול הוא בעצמו ליטול, ואפ"ה שרי הוא בעצמו ליטול, אף על גב דלא הוי כלאחר יד. ויש לומר: דאי לא אשמעינן בחבירו, הוי סלקא דעתך דלא שרינן לחבריה ליטול כדי שיעבוד חבירו:
Tosafot on Eruvin 103b:5:1.english: "Where a bite grew on his back" - It is puzzling, for let [the baraita] teach us an even greater novelty: such as where it grew in a place where he himself is able to remove [it], and even so it is permitted for him to remove [it] himself, even though it is not [done] in a back-handed manner [kilaḥar yad]. And one can say that had it not taught us [the case of] his fellow, it would have entered our minds that we do not permit his fellow to remove [it] in order that his fellow may perform the [Temple] service.

Tosafot on Eruvin 103b:6:1.hebrew: הכי גרסינן ואי רבנן נשקליה ביד ותפשוט דר' אלעזר - פירוש: דשמעינן מינה תרתי — חדא, דמכשירי מצוה לא דחו אב מלאכה; ועוד, דשמעינן דבכלי מודו דחייב חטאת. אבל השתא, לא מצינו למיפשטיה ולמידק דבכלי לא משום דאב מלאכה היא, דהא ביד נמי שבות הוא, ולא קשרו:
Tosafot on Eruvin 103b:6:1.english: This is our reading: "And if [it is according to] the Rabbis, let him remove it by hand, and resolve [the dilemma of] Rabbi Elazar" - Explanation: For we would learn two things from it: one, that preparatory acts for a mitzvah do not override a primary category of labor; and furthermore, that we learn that with an instrument [the Rabbis] agree that he is liable to bring a sin-offering. However, now, we cannot resolve it and infer that [removal] with an instrument is [prohibited] because it is a primary category of labor, for [removing it] by hand is also [only] a rabbinic prohibition, and yet they did not permit it.

Tosafot on Eruvin 103b:7:1.hebrew: אא"ב ר' אליעזר - פי': כי היכי דמשנינן מאב מלאכה לשבות, משנינן נמי משבות חמור לשבות הקל. אלא אי אמרת רבנן, למה להו לאהדורי (אלא) אשבות כל דהו? והקשה השר מקוצי, דאמאי ניחא ליה למיעבד הרחקה לר"א טפי מלרבנן? והיה נראה להפך, דהא ר"א מיקל טפי! ותירץ, דהיא הנותנת: אליבא דרבנן יש להתיר כל שבות דלא נפיק מינה חורבה, כיון דאית להו דמשום הכשר לא דחינן שבת; אבל רי אליעזר, דאית ליה דמכשירי' דוחה, ומיהו באפשר לשנויי משנינן — יש לנו לחזר אחר שבות הקל, שלא יבא להתיר בלא שינוי באפשר לשנויי:
Tosafot on Eruvin 103b:7:1.english: "Granted, if you say [it is] Rabbi Eliezer" - Explanation: Just as we deviate from a primary category of labor to a rabbinic prohibition, we also deviate from a stringent rabbinic prohibition to a lenient rabbinic prohibition. However, if you say [it is in accordance with] the Rabbis, why would they seek out (only) any [lighter] rabbinic prohibition? And the Sar of Coucy raised a difficulty: Why is it preferable to make a distancing [preventive decree] according to Rabbi Eliezer more than according to the Rabbis? And it would seem [that it should be] the opposite, for Rabbi Eliezer is more lenient! And he answered that this is the very reason: According to the Rabbis, any rabbinic prohibition from which no ruin will result may be permitted, since they hold that for the sake of preparation [of a mitzvah] we do not override Shabbat; but according to Rabbi Eliezer, who holds that accessories [of a mitzvah] override [Shabbat], and yet when it is possible to deviate, we deviate — we must seek out the lighter rabbinic prohibition, lest one come to permit [performing the act] without a deviation when it is possible to deviate.
